transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, uh… I guess the main thing is people keep telling me I’m not listening. Like my supervisor will be talking right at me, or my wife at home, and I’ll be looking at them, you know, like I’m there, and then a minute later I realize I only caught maybe half of what they said.

Then I’m asking them to repeat it, and they get frustrated—especially at work, because there’s noise and machines and, well, there’s always something going on. But even when it’s just my wife talking to me, it happens. That’s really what pushed me to come in, because it’s been causing problems.

Have you noticed any difficulty actually hearing sounds clearly—like needing the TV or radio louder than others prefer, or missing things like the doorbell or phone ringing—separate from just losing track of what someone is saying?

I don’t think so… I mean, I haven’t really noticed it like that. The TV thing, I don’t know—sometimes my wife says it’s too loud, but then she also says that about the blender, and we’ve got this old TV in the living room that the volume jumps around anyway, so I don’t know if that counts.

Like, I hear the phone if it rings, usually. Doorbell too, unless I’m in the garage and the washer’s going or something. It feels more like I hear the person talking, but then my brain kind of… wanders off, or I miss what they meant. But actual hearing? I don’t think I’ve had a problem with that.
Thinking back to when you were a kid in school, did teachers or family ever say you had trouble paying attention, staying focused, or finishing tasks?

Yeah, yeah, that goes way back. I mean, school was… I wasn’t exactly the quiet kid. Teachers were always moving my seat around, like putting me up front or away from other kids, because I couldn’t stay put and I’d be messing with stuff or turning around.

And I used to call out answers a lot—like before they even finished asking sometimes. I remember getting in trouble for that. Or I’d jump into what another kid was doing, like trying to help or tell them how to do it, and then suddenly I’m the one in trouble for butting in. This was pretty early, like before middle school for sure.

Since childhood, would you say these attention and restlessness issues have been present pretty much continuously through your teens and into adulthood, or was there a period where they went away and then came back?

I’m not totally sure how to separate it out, honestly. Like, I don’t remember a time where I suddenly became a totally different, calm, focused person or anything… but it’s hard to say it in a straight line, you know?

In high school I was working part-time too, and there was always stuff going on, and then after school I went right into jobs where you’re moving around a lot, so maybe it didn’t stand out the same way. I kind of just thought that was how I was. But whether it “went away” and came back… I don’t think I’d put it that way. It’s more like some times it caused more trouble than other times.
Can you tell me about a specific recent example of how this inattentiveness has caused a problem at work, and another example of how it's caused a problem at home?

Yeah, um… at work, the recent one that kind of scared me was on the line. I missed part of what I was supposed to be keeping track of, and it turned into this whole thing where the supervisor had to pull me aside. I’ve had formal warnings now, like written ones, and that’s… I mean, that’s not just “oops, I forgot.” I do worry I’m going to lose the job if I keep messing up, or worse, miss something that causes a safety issue. There’s machinery and people moving around, and you can’t really be half-there.

At home, it’s more like… my wife will have a routine going with the kids, getting dinner or bedtime or everyone out the door, and I’m supposed to be helping, but I’ll get sidetracked or jump into the wrong thing and throw it off. Then everyone’s frustrated because instead of making it smoother, I’ve kind of made more chaos. And then I feel bad, because I’m not trying to make it harder for them.
How would you describe your sleep lately—do you feel rested when you wake up, and have you or your wife noticed any loud snoring, gasping, or pauses in your breathing at night?

Sleep? Uh… I mean, it’s kind of all over the place, but I don’t know if I’d say anything specific like that. Some mornings I’m okay, some mornings I feel like I got hit by a truck, but that might just be the schedule and the kids and, you know, work days starting early.

As far as snoring or gasping or stopping breathing… I don’t think my wife has said anything like that to me. Or if she has, it wasn’t like a big “you need to get checked” thing. I guess I haven’t really paid close attention. I can ask her, though, because she’d probably know better than me.
Over the past several months, have you been feeling down, anxious, or excessively worried much of the time, in a way that's separate from the frustration you feel about these attention issues?

I don’t know… I mean, I get stressed, for sure. Like when work is on me or at home when I’ve messed up the whole routine, I’ll feel pretty lousy about it.

But if you mean like down or worried all the time on its own, separate from that… I’m not sure I’d say that. It’s kind of hard to separate, because once one thing goes sideways, then I’m thinking about money, the kids, whether I forgot something, and then I’m off on this whole chain. Like yesterday I was trying to fix something in the garage and ended up reorganizing a shelf instead, and then my wife asked about dinner and I realized I’d totally lost track of time—so then I’m annoyed at myself, not necessarily “depressed,” if that makes sense.

So… yeah, I don’t really know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a separate thing like that, but I do get frustrated and stressed when things pile up.
Right now, as an adult, do you still notice things like feeling restless or fidgety, having trouble sitting still, or blurting things out or interrupting people?

Yeah, the restless part, definitely. Like if I have to sit still, it’s not just “I’m bored.” It feels like pressure building up, kind of in my chest and my legs, like I need to move or do something right now or I’m gonna crawl out of my skin.

Even sitting here talking about it, I’m thinking about how long I’ve been sitting, and then I start noticing the chair, and my legs want to go. It’s weird because I’ll tell myself, “Just sit still, you’re a grown man,” but my body’s already like… no, get up, move, do something.
Do you still find yourself interrupting others in conversation or blurting out comments before they've finished speaking, even now as an adult?

Yeah… I do, but it’s not always just talking over people, though that happens too. At work it’s more like I’ll jump into somebody else’s setup before they’ve asked me. Like I’ll see a coworker doing something and my brain goes, “No, no, move that over there,” and before I know it I’m reaching in or telling them how to do it.

Then they get mad because, yeah, I didn’t wait my turn or let them finish. And I get it after the fact, but in the moment it feels like I have to fix it right then. It’s caused arguments, because I come off like I’m bossing people around or butting in.
